expected: After step 1: Driver is online and the Home Screen is visible. After step 2: Destination filter is active; the app UI reflects that the filter is currently applied. After step 3: The API returns a successful response (200 OK) but with an empty offers array and the destination filter status metadata. After step 4: The Radar List screen opens. After step 5: The screen displays a specific 'Destination Filter' empty state, including the designated visual assets (icon/illustration) and a text message informing the driver that no rides are available matching their destination. After step 6: The API is re-called; the 'Destination Filter' empty state remains visible as long as the filter is active and no matching rides exist.

title: Low Demand Area Empty State Display
folder: Jeeny Radar
steps: Set the driver's status to 'Online' and ensure 'is_busy' is false. Configure the backend/mock server for the [GET] /driver/radar-offers/{driverId} endpoint to return an empty list with the specific reason code or payload for 'low demand area'. Tap on the Jeeny Radar icon on the home screen to open the radar list. Observe the UI when the API response is received. Perform a manual refresh on the empty state screen.
expected: After step 1: The driver is active on the home screen and eligible to receive ride offers. After step 2: The API is prepared to simulate a scenario where no rides are available in the driver's current location. After step 3: The Radar List screen opens and initiates a request to the radar-offers API. After step 4: The screen does not show any ride cards; instead, it displays the 'Low Demand Area' empty state, including the designated illustration and a message informing the driver that there are currently no requests in their vicinity. After step 5: The app re-calls the radar-offers API; if the state remains the same, the 'Low Demand Area' empty state persists without UI glitches.

title: Empty State Priority - Low Balance vs Low Demand
folder: Jeeny Radar
steps: Log in to the driver application with an account that has a wallet balance below the minimum required threshold. Position the driver in a geographical area designated as a 'Low Demand Area' where no active ride offers are available. Set the driver status to 'Online' and ensure 'is_busy' is false. Tap on the Jeeny Radar / Ride Finder icon on the Home Screen to open the radar list. Observe the empty state message displayed on the screen. Verify that the 'Low Balance' screen provides the appropriate call-to-action (e.g., a button to top up the wallet).
expected: After step 1: Driver is logged in successfully; backend identifies 'is_ride_balance_verified' as false. After step 2: System state reflects both a low balance condition and a lack of available ride offers. After step 3: The driver is eligible to receive radar updates. After step 4: The app calls the [GET] /driver/radar-offers/{driverId} API. After step 5: The UI displays the 'Low Balance' empty state (is_ride_balance_verified: false) instead of the 'Low Demand' message, as financial eligibility is the primary blocker. After step 6: The driver is prompted to resolve the balance issue to proceed.

title: Transition from Empty State to Active Offers
folder: Jeeny Radar
steps: Ensure the driver is online, 'is_busy' is false, and the backend is currently returning an empty list with the 'low demand area' status for the radar-offers API. Trigger a backend state change so that the next call to [GET] /driver/radar-offers/{driverId} returns a valid list of 1 or more ride offers. Perform a manual refresh on the Radar List screen or wait for the automatic polling/socket update to trigger the API call. Observe the UI transition on the Radar List screen. Verify the content of the newly appeared cards.
expected: After step 1: The Radar List screen displays the 'Low Demand Area' empty state message/illustration. After step 2: The backend successfully updates the radar_offer_count and provides valid offer objects. After step 3: The app calls the radar-offers API and receives a 200 OK response with the new offer data. After step 4: The 'Low Demand' empty state immediately disappears and is replaced by the scrollable list of active ride offer cards. After step 5: Each card correctly displays Pickup/Drop-off locations, Service type, ETA, Distance, Fare estimate, and the 'Interested' CTA button.

title: Push Notification Trigger in Background State
folder: Jeeny Radar
steps: Log in to the Jeeny Driver app and set the driver status to 'Online'. Wait for the Radar icon to appear and tap it to open the Radar List. Tap the 'Interested' CTA button on a specific ride offer card. Immediately minimize the app to move it to the background (do not kill the process). Trigger a ride match for this driver via the backend/socket (simulating the driver winning the race for the 'interested' offer). Observe the mobile device's notification tray/lock screen.
expected: After step 1: Driver is online and the Home Screen is visible. After step 2: The Radar List opens, displaying available ride offer cards. After step 3: The button state updates to 'Processing' or similar, indicating the interest has been registered via the /offer-update API. After step 4: The mobile device home screen is visible; the app is running in the background. After step 5: The backend sends a socket update/push payload indicating the ride has been successfully matched to the driver. After step 6: A system-level push notification appears informing the driver that the offer has been matched.

title: Ride Acceptance via Push Notification Interaction
folder: Jeeny Radar
steps: Log in to the driver app, go online, and ensure the driver is not busy (is_busy = false). Open the Jeeny Radar list and tap the 'Interested' CTA button on an available ride offer. Immediately move the application to the background or lock the device screen. Wait for the backend to process the match and send an in-app push notification indicating the offer is ready for acceptance. Tap on the received push notification. Observe the application screen and verify the API response.
expected: After step 1: The driver is online and the Home Screen is visible. After step 2: The /api/v1/driver/offer-update API is called with 'is_interested: true' and the card state updates to 'Processing' or similar. After step 3: The application is no longer in the foreground. After step 4: A push notification for the specific ride offer appears on the device's notification tray/lock screen. After step 5: The app opens/brings to foreground and automatically triggers the /ride-accept API call including the 'is_interested' flag. After step 6: The 'Offer Matched' screen is displayed for the duration defined in 'matched_offer_screen_show_time' (default 5s) and the ride is successfully assigned to the driver.

title: Driver Goes Offline After Interest Expression
folder: Jeeny Radar
steps: Log in to the Jeeny Driver app and set the status to 'Online'. Tap the Ride Finder icon to open the Radar List. Tap the 'Interested' CTA button on a specific ride card. Immediately navigate back to the Home Screen and toggle the driver status to 'Offline' before the ride matching logic completes. Observe the system behavior and monitor network logs for the /ride-accept call. Wait for the matching duration to conclude.
expected: After step 1: Driver is online; the Ride Finder icon appears when 'radar_offer_count' > 0. After step 2: The list of available ride cards is displayed. After step 3: The [PATCH] /api/v1/driver/offer-update API is triggered with 'is_interested: true'; the button state changes to 'Processing' or similar loading state. After step 4: The driver status is updated to offline; the Ride Finder icon and Radar List are hidden/removed from the UI. After step 5: The /ride-accept call is either not initiated or is rejected by the backend because the driver is no longer in an 'available' state. After step 6: The 'Offer Matched' screen is not displayed, and the driver remains offline without being assigned the trip.

title: Total Connectivity Loss After Interest Expression
folder: Jeeny Radar
steps: Log in to the Jeeny Driver app and go online. Wait for the Radar icon to appear and tap it to open the Radar List. Tap the 'Interested' button on a specific ride card and immediately toggle the device to Airplane Mode (or disable all network connectivity). Observe the app behavior while connectivity is lost for at least 30 seconds. Restore internet connectivity on the device. Check the status of the previously selected ride.
expected: After step 1: Driver is online, 'is_busy' is false, and the Home Screen is visible. After step 2: The Radar List opens, displaying available ride cards with 'Interested' buttons. After step 3: The app attempts to send the [PATCH] /api/v1/driver/offer-update request; the UI should reflect a 'Processing' or loading state for the CTA. After step 4: The app should display a 'No Internet Connection' banner or a retry/timeout error message; the card should not incorrectly transition to 'Offer Matched' without server confirmation. After step 5: The app reconnects to the server; the Radar List should refresh via the [GET] /driver/radar-offers API. After step 6: If the ride was successfully matched on the backend during the brief window, the 'Offer Matched' screen appears; if the request failed or the ride expired, the card is removed or shows as 'Expired'.

title: Push Notification Delivery on Terminated App State
folder: Jeeny Radar
steps: Log in to the Jeeny Driver app and go online. Wait for the Radar icon to appear and tap it to open the Radar List. Tap the 'Interested' CTA button on a specific ride card. Immediately force-close (kill) the application from the OS task switcher. Wait for the backend to match the ride to the driver and send the socket/push notification. Tap on the received push notification. Observe the app behavior immediately after launch.
expected: After step 1: Driver is online and the Home Screen is visible. After step 2: The Radar List opens, displaying available ride offers. After step 3: The button state updates to 'Processing' or similar, and the /api/v1/driver/offer-update request is sent with is_interested: true. After step 4: The application is completely terminated and not running in the background. After step 5: A system push notification is received on the device indicating the ride offer is ready for acceptance. After step 6: The Jeeny Driver app launches successfully from the terminated state. After step 7: The app automatically triggers the /ride-accept API and displays the 'Offer Matched' screen for the duration defined in 'matched_offer_screen_show_time'.

title: Connectivity Loss During Push Notification Interaction
folder: Jeeny Radar
steps: Ensure the driver is logged in, online, and the app is running in the background. Trigger a radar offer for the driver and wait for the in-app push notification to appear on the device. Disable the device's internet connection (e.g., enable Airplane Mode or turn off Wi-Fi/Mobile Data). Tap on the push notification to initiate the ride acceptance process. Observe the application's response to the failed API call due to lack of connectivity. enable the internet connection and check if the app allows a retry or returns the driver to the Home Screen/Radar List.
expected: After step 1: Driver is in a 'ready' state to receive offers while the app is not in the foreground. After step 2: The push notification for the interested offer is received and displayed on the device's notification tray. After step 3: The device is completely offline with no active data connection. After step 4: The app attempts to open and call the /ride-accept API. After step 5: The app displays a clear error message (e.g., 'No internet connection' or 'Request failed') and does not hang on a loading state indefinitely. After step 6: The app gracefully handles the transition, allowing the driver to see the current state of the radar or showing that the specific offer is no longer available.

title: Race Condition: Background to Foreground Transition during Update
folder: Jeeny Radar
steps: Ensure the driver is online, not busy, and has previously clicked 'Interested' on a radar offer. Move the Jeeny Driver app to the background (home screen or another app). Trigger a ride-match success or failure via the backend/socket while simultaneously bringing the app to the foreground. Observe the device for system-level push notifications and the in-app UI behavior. Verify that no duplicate alerts (both push and in-app) are presented to the driver at the same time.
expected: After step 1: Driver state is active and waiting for the ride-matching result from the backend. After step 2: The app is running in the background state. After step 3: The app transitions to the foreground state at the moment the socket event is received. After step 4: The system-level push notification is suppressed or dismissed automatically; the in-app 'Offer Matched' screen (or 'Not Matched' notification) is displayed immediately. After step 5: Only one notification/screen is visible, ensuring a clean UI transition without redundant alerts.

title: Event Emission - Multiple Cards Rendered
folder: Jeeny Radar
steps: Ensure the driver is online, not busy, and has at least 3 available ride offers in the radar queue. Open the mobile app debugging tool or proxy (e.g., Charles Proxy or Logcat) to monitor outgoing analytics events. Tap on the Ride Finder icon to open the Radar List view. Observe the captured events in the debugging tool as the cards render on the screen. Verify the payload of each 'radar_presented' event. Scroll down if there are more cards (up to the max limit of 5) that were not initially visible.
expected: After step 1: The Home Screen displays the Ride Finder icon with a badge count reflecting the available offers. After step 2: The debugger is active and ready to capture network/event traffic. After step 3: The Radar List opens, displaying multiple ride cards (e.g., 3 cards) sorted by ETA. After step 4: The app emits a unique 'radar_presented' event for every individual card currently visible in the list. After step 5: Each event contains the specific identifier (e.g., ride_id or radar_offer_identifier) corresponding to the card that was rendered. After step 6: As new cards enter the viewport, additional 'radar_presented' events are emitted for those specific cards.

title: UI Robustness - Text Overflow
folder: Jeeny Radar
steps: Log in to the driver application and set the driver status to 'Online'. Mock or trigger a Radar offer via the backend with an extremely long Pickup address (e.g., 200+ characters) and a long Service Type name. Tap on the Ride Finder icon to open the Radar List. Observe the Pickup and Drop-off address fields on the card. Observe the Service Type label on the card. Verify the overall card dimensions and alignment.
expected: After step 1: Driver is online and ready to receive ride offers. After step 2: The 'radar_offer_count' increments and the Ride Finder icon appears on the Home Screen. After step 3: The Radar List opens, displaying the card with the long address and service type strings. After step 4: Text does not overlap with other UI elements (like ETA or Fare). Long addresses are either truncated with ellipses (...) or wrapped to a new line according to design specifications. After step 5: The Service Type text is contained within its designated area without breaking the card's container or overlapping the 'Interested' button. After step 6: The card maintains a consistent width and height relative to other cards; the layout remains functional and visually professional despite the long text input.

title: UI Performance - Rapid Refresh Stress Test
folder: Jeeny Radar
steps: Log in to the driver app and set the status to 'Online'. Ensure there are active radar offers available and tap the Ride Finder icon to open the Radar List. Perform a manual refresh (pull-to-refresh or tap refresh button) 5 to 10 times in rapid succession (less than 0.5 seconds between taps). Observe the loading indicator behavior during the rapid refresh actions. Wait for the final refresh to complete and attempt to scroll through the list and tap an 'Interested' button. Verify the data displayed on the cards after the stress test.
expected: After step 1: The driver is online and the Home Screen is visible. After step 2: The Radar List opens, displaying available ride cards sorted by ETA. After step 3: The application remains stable without crashing; the UI does not flicker excessively or show overlapping card data. After step 4: The loading indicator appears and disappears smoothly, or stays active until the final request is resolved, without freezing the interface. After step 5: The list is scrollable, and the 'Interested' CTA remains functional and responsive to touch. After step 6: Card details (Pickup/Drop-off, ETA, Fare) are correctly rendered and match the latest data from the /driver/radar-offers API.

title: Radar Icon Visibility - Missing Offer Count
folder: Jeeny Radar
steps: Ensure the driver is logged into the mobile app and set to 'Online' status. Intercept or mock the [PUT] /taxi-position/v3 API response to ensure the 'radar_offer_count' field is completely missing from the JSON payload. After step 2: The API returns a 200 OK status, but the 'radar_offer_count' key is absent. After step 3: The Radar/Ride Finder icon is not visible on the Home Screen.
